extracted.intended_audience: Users of Isabelle/HOL (theorem-proving / formal methods practitioners writing specifications, inductive definitions, recursive functions, records, and types)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for defining inductive/coinductive predicates, recursive and partial functions, records, type definitions, and related proof obligations in Isabelle/HOL. Covers command semantics, syntactic constraints, required proof obligations (monotonicity, termination, domain proofs), and derived theorems/tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inductive definition principle
rubrics_metrics.description: An inductive definition specifies the least predicate or set R closed under given rules: applying a rule to elements of R yields a result within R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inductive definitions are used to formalize structural notions (e.g., operational semantics). They rely on the Knaster-Tarski fixed-point theorem; the user-provided introduction rules determine a functor on subsets and monotonicity must be proven for operators applied to recursive occurrences. The default Isabelle/HOL rule declarations handle most common situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coinductive definition principle
rubrics_metrics.description: A coinductive definition specifies the greatest predicate or set R that is consistent with given rules: every element of R can be seen as arising by applying a rule to elements of R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for bisimulation/equivalence of processes and infinite data structures. Also based on Knaster-Tarski fixed-point theorem; requires monotonicity proofs for the recursion scheme analogous to inductive definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: (co)inductive where-clause format and abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: The propositions given as clauses in the where part are either rules of the usual (…)/=⇒ format (with arbitrary nesting), or equalities using ≡.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equalities using ≡ specify extra-logical abbreviations (abbreviation). Introducing abstract syntax simultaneously with introduction rules can be useful for complex specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: for and monos options for (co)inductive
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional for part contains a list of parameters of the (co)inductive predicates that remain fixed throughout the definition; optional monos declaration contains additional monotonicity theorems required for operators applied to recursive sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use monos to declare extra monotonicity theorems when the default set is insufficient; 'for' distinguishes fixed parameters from varying arguments in clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: (co)inductive derived theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: A (co)inductive definition of R provides R.intros (list of introduction rules), R.cases (case analysis/elimination rule), R.induct or R.coinduct ((co)induction rule), and R.simps (equation unrolling the fixpoint one step).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When defining several predicates simultaneously names are combined: R1_. . ._Rn.intros, R1.cases, . . . etc. Individual introduction rules are also available by the names given in the theory file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity theorem format
rubrics_metrics.description: Monotonicity theorems used to prove monotonicity have the general form A ≤ B =⇒ M A ≤ M B for operators M occurring around recursive occurrences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The context maintains a default set of theorems for monotonicity proofs; new rules can be declared via the mono attribute. Provide monotonicity proofs for each operator applied to the recursive set in introduction rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical-operator monotonicity and polarity equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Monotonicity theorems for logical operators are of the general form (… −→ …) =⇒ … −→ …. Also provide De Morgan style equations for polarity reasoning (e.g., ¬¬P ←→ P, ¬(P ∧ Q) ←→ ¬P ∨ ¬Q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include equations reducing complex operators to primitive ones (e.g., (P −→ Q) ←→ ¬P ∨ Q) to facilitate monotonicity proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: print_inductives and mono commands
rubrics_metrics.description: print_inductives prints (co)inductive definitions and monotonicity rules; mono declares monotonicity rules in the context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use print_inductives for inspection and the '!' option to increase verbosity. Declare additional monotonicity rules with mono to help the automated monotonicity proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: primrec equation shape and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each primrec equation must be of the form f x1 … xm (C y1 … yk) z1 … zn = rhs where C is a datatype constructor, rhs contains only free variables on the left-hand side (or from context), and all recursive occurrences of f in rhs are of the form f … yi …. At most one reduction rule per constructor can be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order of equations does not matter. Missing constructors lead to a default value (hard to access). Reduction rules are declared simp by default to enable automation (simp, auto) to normalize f applied to datatype constructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: function package: well-founded recursion and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: function defines functions by general well-founded recursion. The command generates proof obligations for completeness and compatibility of patterns. The defined function is considered partial, with simplification rules f.psimps and induction rule f.pinduct guarded by a generated domain predicate f_dom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use termination to show totality. See referenced literature for detailed examples. 'fun' is shorthand for function (sequential) with automated attempts for pattern matching and termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: function options: sequential
rubrics_metrics.description: sequential enables a preprocessor that disambiguates overlapping patterns by making them mutually disjoint; earlier equations take precedence over later ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resulting simpliﬁcation and induction rules correspond to the transformed specification, not the one given originally; each user equation may yield several theorems. Transformation works for ML-style datatype patterns only.

rubrics_metrics.name: function options: domintros
rubrics_metrics.description: domintros enables automated generation of introduction rules for the domain predicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While mostly not needed, domintros can be helpful in proofs about partial functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: fun_cases elimination rules
rubrics_metrics.description: fun_cases generates specialized elimination rules for function equations; expects function equations and produces rules that eliminate the given equalities following function definition cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fun_cases to get case-based elimination rules aligned with the function's pattern structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induction principles for recursive definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recursive definitions introduced by function accommodate reasoning by induction: rule f.induct refers to a specific induction rule with parameters named according to the user-specified equations; for primrec the induction principle coincides with structural recursion on the datatype.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equations are available as theorem lists f.simps; individual equations may be named explicitly. Cases are numbered starting from 1 for mutual definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: pat_completeness method for pattern matching
rubrics_metrics.description: pat_completeness is a specialized method to solve goals regarding the completeness of pattern matching, as required by the function package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pat_completeness when the function package requires proof that patterns cover all cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: termination proof methods: relation
rubrics_metrics.description: relation R introduces a termination proof using the relation R, producing goals that express R is wellfounded and arguments of recursive calls decrease with respect to R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically used as the initial step in manual termination proofs; the resulting proof state makes the required obligations explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: termination proof methods: lexicographic_order
rubrics_metrics.description: lexicographic_order attempts a fully automated termination proof by searching for a lexicographic combination of size measures on the function arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts the same arguments as auto and clasimpmod modifiers; prints extensive information on failure to help analysis. Useful for automated termination discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: termination proof methods: size_change
rubrics_metrics.description: size_change works on termination goals using a variation of the size-change principle and graph decomposition. It uses max, min, and ms (multiset) orders internally and employs SAT solving internally when searching for a termination proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no orders are given they are tried in order; clasimpmod modifiers are accepted for local descent proofs. Useful for complex termination patterns and possibly infinite-branching situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: termination_simp utility
rubrics_metrics.description: termination_simp declares extra rules for the simplifier to be used in termination proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for special rules involving size estimations or domain-specific simplifications that aid automated termination methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: induction_schema utility
rubrics_metrics.description: induction_schema derives user-specified induction rules from well-founded induction and completeness of patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors out operations done internally by the function package and makes derived induction schemata available separately; see examples in the standard theory for usage patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: partial_function definition approach
rubrics_metrics.description: partial_function (mode) defines recursive functions based on fixpoints in complete partial orders; no termination proof is required and non-termination is modelled explicitly in the result type (with a bottom element).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pattern matching and mutual recursion are not supported; specification is a single recursive equation. The induced functional must be provably monotonic w.r.t. the underlying order; monotonicity is proved internally and the definition is rejected if it fails. Use partial_function_mono to influence monotonicity proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: partial_function operation modes
rubrics_metrics.description: Modes specify the partiality model: option (uses option type with None modelling non-termination) and tailrec (undeﬁned is bottom; requires tail-call structure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: option: monotonicity requires that None returned by recursive call forces overall None — typically achieved via Option.bind. tailrec: permits arbitrary result type but monotonicity typically requires every recursive call to be a tail-call whose result is directly returned. Experienced users may define new modes by instantiating the appropriate locale.

rubrics_metrics.name: partial_function_mono attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: partial_function_mono declares rules for use in internal monotonicity proofs of partial function definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add hints here when the automatic monotonicity proof needs extra lemmas to succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: recdef (TFL) obsolescence and hints
rubrics_metrics.description: The old TFL command recdef for defining recursive functions is mostly obsolete; function or fun should be used instead. recdef supports options like (permissive) and hints such as recdef_simp, recdef_cong, and recdef_wf to guide the internal proof process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recdef only for legacy developments; provide appropriate hints and clasimpmod declarations when necessary to tune simplifier and classical reasoner context.

rubrics_metrics.name: specification command behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: specification decls φ sets up a goal stating the existence of terms with the properties specified for the constants in decls. After finishing the proof, the theory is augmented with definitions for the given constants and theorems stating their properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: decl declares a constant to be defined by the specification; the definition for constant c is bound to c_def unless a theorem name is given. Overloaded constants should be declared as overloaded in the declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: old_rep_datatype deprecation
rubrics_metrics.description: old_rep_datatype represents existing types as old-style datatypes but is mostly obsolete; datatype should be used instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the modern datatype command to obtain proper proof methods for case analysis and induction; see examples and emulate ML tactics via the provided packages if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: record type declaration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Record types must be defined explicitly, fixing their field names and types, and optional parent record. At least one new field must be specified; field names must belong to a unique record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The parent record specification is optional (root records). Type variables of parent and fields must be covered by the record parameters. Record hierarchy forms a forest; there is no way to merge multiple parent records. Use the record package to get selectors, updates, and other operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: records: more part and extensibility constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Record schemes include an improper 'more' field representing further fields (row variable); fixed records are instances where 'more' is unit. The more part is internalized as a free term/type variable; field names are externalized and cannot be first-class values inside the logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensible records enable polymorphic operations over extensions (single inheritance-like behavior). Respect canonical order of fields as declared.

rubrics_metrics.name: record operations and notations
rubrics_metrics.description: Record definitions produce selectors ci, update functions ci_update, cumulative constructor t.make, and extension/truncation operations t.fields, t.extend, t.truncate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updates use postfix notation r(|x := a|); repeated updates are function applications so field order is logically irrelevant. Use t.fields/t.extend/t.truncate for derived record manipulations; t.make and t.fields coincide for root records.

rubrics_metrics.name: record-derived rules for automation
rubrics_metrics.description: The record package declares conversions and canonical forms that integrate with Simpliﬁer and Classical Reasoner: t.simps (selector/update conversions), automatic reduction of selectors on updates, t.iifs (inject equations as iff rules), t.equality (introduction for record equality), and canonical constructor representations for cases/induct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These derived rules enable proofs with simp and generic proof methods (cases, induct) without further setup. Derived operations like t.make, t.fields, t.extend, t.truncate usually need manual expansion via t.defs.

rubrics_metrics.name: typedef semantic subtype requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: typedef identifies a new type with a non-empty subset A :: τ set of an existing type τ, and requires proving ∃x. x ∈ A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new type constructor (α1,…,αn) t is produced depending on type variables. New functions are postulated to establish an isomorphism between the new type and the subset; the type definition must provide the witness to non-emptiness.
